profile.behavior: Forages actively in shallow water with a high-stepping walk, swift bill-stabs, and occasional runs after fish or aquatic invertebrates; often solitary or in loose groups.
field_marks: Very long, bright yellow to orange-yellow legs
Long, dark, slightly upturned bill with a sturdy base
Tall, lanky proportions with a long neck and small head
Dark gray-brown upperparts and folded wings with crisp pale spotting or checkering
Finely streaked head and neck with a distinct pale eye-ring
White belly, variably marked flanks, and a short, dark-barred white tail
profile.habitat: Breeds in boreal bogs, wet meadows, sedgelands, and wet forest clearings; otherwise occupies shallow fresh, brackish, and coastal wetlands such as marshes, mudflats, pond edges, estuaries, and flooded fields.

findings: The common name, scientific name, and family are correctly rendered as “Greater Yellowlegs,” “Tringa melanoleuca,” and “Scolopacidae.”

The printed length 28–38 cm, wingspan 66–74 cm, and weight 105–210 g exactly match Audubon’s published ranges. Cornell currently publishes different measurement ranges, reflecting source variation rather than an internal plate error.

The primary specimen matches Greater Yellowlegs in its tall, small-headed and long-necked proportions; very long yellow legs; dark, long, sturdy-based bill; gray-brown checkered upperparts; streaked head and neck; pale eye-ring; white underparts; and short barred pale tail.

Both depicted heads have coherent, complete mandibles from shared base to co-terminal tip. Their bills are long and subtly upturned without a reversed or exaggerated projection; unequal mandible length is not established as a field mark for this species.

The primary bird has one head, one bill, two anatomically coherent wings with the far folded wing naturally overlapped, two legs with plausible joints and feet, and one tail. No duplicated or malformed attached parts are present.

The detached wing and head/bill drawings are clearly separated supplementary studies. Their feather structure, eye placement, and bill proportions are consistent with the primary specimen and reference photographs.

The habitat and behavior passages agree with the direct sources: boreal wetland breeding habitat, varied shallow wetlands outside breeding, active shallow-water foraging, high-stepping walking, running after prey, swift bill-stabs, and generally solitary or loose-group behavior.
All six printed field-mark statements match the proposed wording and verified traits. No duplicated, omitted, substituted, misspelled, or nonsensical words were found.

The vertical range ruler is internally consistent: 28 cm is at the bottom, 38 cm at the top, exactly four evenly spaced unlabeled interior ticks create five proportional segments, and the separate “BODY LENGTH: 28–38 cm” marker agrees with it. “SCHEMATIC — NOT TO SCALE” prevents presentation as the printed bird’s physical size.
The five swatches correspond recognizably to bright yellow, charcoal black, slate gray, earth brown, and white.
No place name, ZIP code, coordinates, map, or local-observation detail appears.
